method.grouping: Analyst-defined action situations, inspired by IAD / networks of adjacent action situations. These are not official departments or a complete formal IAD model.
method.provenance: Base institutional claims are inherited from the v0.3 desk-research model. New scope and institutional-mode tags are editorial classifications, not independent source verification. No stakeholder validation is claimed.
method.missing: Unknown is not false. No budget amounts, influence scores or observed compliance have been inferred.

citations.title: McGinnis (2011), Networks of Adjacent Action Situations in Polycentric Governance
W3C PROV-O: provenance entities, activities and agents

nodes.label: Planting stock
nodes.summary: Trees supplied by nurseries for planting. This represents planting material, not a measured stock or purchasing commitment.
nodes.why: Makes the material input to planting explicit.

nodes.label: Operational capacity
nodes.summary: Staff time and contracted tree-care capacity. Its enabling role is a modelling synthesis; no staffing totals, available hours or budget allocations have been established.
nodes.why: Distinguishes a management instruction from the capacity needed to carry it out.

nodes.label: Municipal replant fund
nodes.summary: The gemeentelijk herplantfonds receives financial compensation where physical replacement cannot be achieved under the applicable policy. Funds can support planting elsewhere; this is not the general budget for all tree care.
nodes.why: Separates a financial mechanism from the planting activity it can support.

edges.label: supplies planting stock
edges.evidence: Route van de boom, part 1, describes nursery origins and tree selection.

edges.label: provides planting material
edges.evidence: Route van de boom, parts 1-2, describe nursery trees and preparing a growing place.

edges.label: can contribute contracted capacity
edges.evidence: Analytical resource abstraction from the specialist contract role. Capacity has not been measured.

edges.label: enables execution of tree care
edges.evidence: An enabling relationship, not proof that capacity is sufficient or allocated to any particular task.

edges.label: can require financial compensation
edges.evidence: Compensatie en herplant, sections on financial compensation and the municipal replant fund. Conditional on the applicable permit and replacement possibilities.

edges.label: can fund eligible planting elsewhere
edges.evidence: Compensatie en herplant, Gemeentelijk herplantfonds: compensation can be used for planting elsewhere in the city. Not all planting is funded this way.

actionSituations.label: Policy & standards
actionSituations.question: How do city objectives become requirements for tree management?
actionSituations.summary: Strategic objectives, public-space standards and executive implementation. This grouping distinguishes policy direction from a binding permit condition.
gaps: How are competing objectives translated into a funded work programme?
Which policy requirements are checked in operational contracts?
outcomes: Management priorities and applicable standards; not a single official procedure.

actionSituations.label: Project & site design
actionSituations.question: Can a project retain existing trees and provide viable growing places?
actionSituations.summary: Project planning, tree-impact assessment and species/site design. The BEA informs choices; it is not itself permission to remove a tree.
gaps: Who resolves conflicts between tree retention and other project objectives?
Which site constraints and alternatives are actually recorded?
outcomes: Design choices and BEA evidence for subsequent assessment.

actionSituations.label: Permit decisions
actionSituations.question: Who can approve a major intervention, on what advice and conditions?
actionSituations.summary: The formal permit route, specialist advice, decisions and objections. District and ODNZKG roles are alternatives depending on area, not successive approval steps.
gaps: Check the competent authority and applicable exceptions for a specific case.
The general graph does not establish whether a particular resident has standing to object.
outcomes: A permit decision, refusal, or conditions; an application is not an approval.

actionSituations.label: Planting, care & replacement
actionSituations.question: What turns a decision into care, replacement or a new tree?
actionSituations.summary: Establishment, routine care and major interventions are different operational routes. Activities shown here are not a compulsory chronological sequence.
gaps: Staff capacity, contract allocations and budgets have not been measured.
A replanting obligation is not evidence that replacement has been completed.
outcomes: Physical tree work and replacement obligations; ecological recovery may take years.

actionSituations.label: Reports & assessment
actionSituations.question: How do an observation or a public report reach a management decision?
actionSituations.summary: Resident reports and routine inspection enter through different routes. Records, specialist assessment and management decisions connect observations to work or a permit referral.
gaps: The existence of a dataset does not prove it was used in an individual decision.
Response times, escalation criteria and case outcomes need empirical validation.
outcomes: An assessment, a work instruction or referral to the permit process.

actionSituations.label: Outcomes & learning
actionSituations.question: Does monitoring change future policy or day-to-day management?
actionSituations.summary: City-level green indicators, ecological monitoring and public tree accounting. These are different evidence streams; canopy cover is not a biodiversity measure by itself.
gaps: The monitoring-to-policy feedback relation is a synthesis, not a verified closed loop.
Permit accounting, completed planting and ecological outcomes must not be treated as equivalent.
outcomes: Indicators and accountability records; feedback into policy is an explicit research question.
